chemicalCases.reason: The dry addition gives R-NH-C(=O)-O-R-prime with no eliminated water. Joining terminal carbonyl to the next unit oxygen makes the supplied repeat valence-correct. L has 200 mol OH and200 mol NCO; N has180+30=210 mol OH and210 mol NCO. Bifunctional components permit linear chains; triol introduces branching and network formation at sufficient conversion. Adhesive suitability is conditional; stoichiometric equality alone does not prove adhesion or useful service temperature.

Summing the given equations yields2 isocyanate groups per water molecule and one CO2. For the explicitly complete route 2 mmol H2O gives2 mmol CO2 and consumes4 mmol NCO, leaving96 mmol as the upper availability for alcohol before competing reactions. Gas bubbles support the moisture path but cannot establish complete dry polyurethane formation or a good network. The model correctly allows dissolution/gas loss.

A learner can supply every explicit request with a matched dry/moist comparison, explain urethane versus amine/urea, compute 2 mmol CO2, 4 mmol NCO consumed and 96 mmol remaining, and reject bubbles as proof of dry PU success, yet lose full credit because the two additional required elements were not disclosed. The complete-path correction does not remove this assessment mismatch.
